description: A UTF-8 byte order mark before the root value is an error
notes: RFC 7159 says that implementations must not add a byte order mark, but that parsers may ignore one instead of treating it as an error (section 8.1). The spec adopts RFC 7159's grammar as-is, which rules out the non-JSON extensions that section 9 lets parsers accept, but the encoding allowances of section 8.1 aren't grammar, so the spec allows both. hashicorp/hcl's JSON scanner treats the mark's first byte as an invalid token (scan in json/scanner.go).
